titulo: Extraction through the subscription and the check that discards
lead: Listing pages, news article bodies, page summaries: the agent writes from a source, in batches. The risk is that it embellishes and makes things up. Here you call the model through the subscription, in read-only mode, read the first JSON in the reply, and run everything through a check that discards the made-up item.
objetivo: call Codex or Claude through the subscription to extract from a source and discard, without fixing, any item that fails the check.

aprende.t: The Codex call in read-only mode, no API
Why read only the first JSON in the reply
The check: title, words, and numbers in the source
Discarding is not losing: it keeps the batch clean

hero_alt: A quality-control technician sorts samples into two steel trays, comparing each one against a reference sheet.

secoes.titulo: From the source to an item that can go live

nos.detalhe: The text of the item's page, saved to a file. If the source requires a login or has little text, the item has nowhere to get facts from and is left out.
Codex runs without write permission (read-only sandbox), in a session that isn't kept (ephemeral), and writes only the last message to a file. No API key involved.
Sometimes the model returns the JSON twice or with text around it. Reading only the first complete object keeps the batch from breaking because of a single reply.

itens.t: every number appears in the source

nos.detalhe: validar_extracao.mjs checks each item. A failed item is discarded, not fixed by hand to make it pass.
A listing page with 3 or more valid modules becomes enriched. One that doesn't reach that is left out or kept with noindex until the source has text.

secoes.legenda: The model can rewrite and organize; the check ensures it didn't create facts.

secoes.titulo: How INEMA does it in batches

texto: INEMA's news text generator calls Codex with the request through standard input, a read-only sandbox, an ephemeral session, and output to a file. Close the input after sending the request: otherwise the process keeps waiting.
In Claude Code, the same request runs in the project folder, with AGENTS.md forbidding writes outside the output folder.
On 10/02/2026, Codex replies with duplicated JSON broke the batch reading. The smallest fix was to read only the first complete object (the primeiroJson function).
It wasn't switching models or rewriting the generator: a ten-line safeguard.

Of the 159 news articles, 113 got a text body. The 46 without text stayed that way because the source requires a login (25), has little text (18), or returned a 404 (1), and they stay with noindex, out of the sitemap.
Nobody wrote the missing parts by hand: better one page fewer than a page with a made-up fact.
The first round of listing pages used an authorized API: 40 listing pages extracted and validated for US$ 0.031. The following batches moved to Codex through the subscription.
The check is the same on both paths; what changes is who pays for the call.

secoes.titulo: The call, the first JSON, and the check on the batch
secoes.sub: pedido.txt = extractive prompt (course 2, lesson 5) + the source text. valida-ficha.mjs is a template that uses the validar_extracao.mjs library.

blocos.conteudo:
codex exec --skip-git-repo-check --ephemeral --sandbox read-only -C "$PWD" -o saida.txt - < pedido.txt
node valida-ficha.mjs fonte.txt saida.txt

secoes.titulo: Practice: an extraction with a check
secoes.sub: Pick an item on your site that has its own page with text.

exercicios.texto: Save the page text in fonte.txt, build the pedido.txt with the extractive prompt, and run the Codex call (or the same request in Claude Code). Repeat with a free-form request, "de forma atraente" (in an attractive way), to compare.
exercicios.pronto: you have saida.txt and saida-livre.txt, both in JSON, and no API key was used.

exercicios.texto: Copy validar_extracao.mjs and valida-ficha.mjs into the folder and run them on both outputs. Write down what was discarded and why.
exercicios.pronto: a note lists each discarded item with the reason (title, words, or number outside the source), and only the listing page with 3 or more valid modules is marked for publishing.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: What is the read-only sandbox option in the Codex call for?
opcoes: So the answer comes out faster.
So the agent does not write or delete anything while it extracts.
To use the API instead of the subscription.
perguntas.explica: Extracting is just reading. Without write permission, a model error does not turn into a changed file. The output goes only to the file you name.

perguntas.p: In the "attractive" prompt, the model wrote "totalizando 24 horas". The source said 8 sessions of 3 hours. What does the check do?
opcoes: It accepts it, because the math is right.
It discards it, because the number 24 does not appear in the source.
perguntas.explica: The check confirms whether the number is in the source, not whether the math adds up. An item with a number outside the source is discarded; fixing it by hand opens the door for the next error to slip through.

perguntas.p: The model's responses came back with duplicated JSON and the batch broke. What was the smallest fix?
opcoes: Read only the first complete JSON object in the response.
perguntas.explica: A few-line safeguard (primeiroJson) solved it. The failure log rule is to look for the smallest fix before rebuilding.

perguntas.p: 46 news items were left without body text because the source required login, had little text, or returned a 404. What was done with them?
opcoes: The agent wrote a generic text.
They stayed noindex and out of the sitemap until they had text.
They were published with the title only.
perguntas.explica: No source, no fact. The page stays out of the index instead of getting made-up text or staying a thin page.

itens.texto: codex exec with a read-only sandbox, an ephemeral session, and output written to a file.
One bad answer can't bring down the whole batch.
Title, words, and numbers are checked against the source; anything that fails is dropped.
Non-commodity content comes from the real page's first-hand data, not from a more "attractive" text.
